title: BofA September spending rises across income cohorts; the selected nominal sample counters broad spending collapse
body:
Bank of America's October9 Consumer Checkpoint reports September card spending per household +6.2% YoY, +5.1% excluding gasoline. The headline YoY basis is not seasonally adjusted. Total SA MoM growth was +0.2%; ex-gas was approximately flat. [Publisher primary](https://institute.bankofamerica.com/content/dam/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-october-2026.pdf), pp1–2.

Reported lower/middle/higher-income cohort growth was 5.5/4.9/4.8%, and top5% growth 5.9%; the cohort charts use three-month averages and seasonal adjustment, not the headline basis. This is nominal spending among active BofA households making at least five card transactions monthly. Sample selection, prices and group definitions prevent an all-household or real-volume conclusion.

This adds observed counterevidence to broad downward spending convergence while leaving concentrated credit stress and weaker survey intentions possible. CARL integrated its own source and retained its registered score; WALTER does not re-grade it. New September observation to BOARD, not another dispatch of the older BofA delinquency or market-allocation items.

**CARL action:** use the dated selected-sample counterevidence in existing consumer evidence; preserve cohort/adjustment limits. HENRY/RED/PROME information. Inline primary verification: retained publisher text lines9–39,326–346,772–800.
caveat: Nominal selected sample; headline and cohort adjustment clocks differ; no universal recovery or grade change.

title: NY Fed tariff model: the earlier inflation pulse fades, but Canadian pass-through and an announced 2027 auto tail remain
corrects: EXTERNAL: CARL KB506 blanket spent-forward-driver gloss of NY Fed October6 tariff study
summary: EXTERNAL CARL KB506 said tariff forward driver spent; IS post-Aug2026 goods-price-level increase and conditional Jan2027 auto-tariff tail (NYFedOct6 model, non-oil goods); earlier pulse fade HOLDS, blanket spent-driver conclusion WEAKEN
body:
The final forecast paragraphs of the New York Fed's October6 study qualify the earlier “spent forward driver” interpretation. The prior tariff contribution to twelve-month consumer-goods inflation peaks at2.9pp inFebruary and fades aroundAugust; that part survives. [Primary study](https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/10/how-fast-do-tariffs-pass-through-into-consumer-prices/), forecast paragraphs/figure notes.

AfterAugust the modeled goods-price-level effect rises again: roughly half from already-enacted Canadian tariffs still passing through, the remainder from the announced January2027 Canadian auto increase. The contribution turns slightly positive bymid2027. The forecast holds end-September tariffs otherwise fixed. It covers non-oil goods, excludes services, and is a research counterfactual, not verified future policy or all-CPI attribution.

Direction: the blanket spent-driver conclusion WEAKENS; the earlier pulse's fade HOLDS. CARL has corrected its own source. **CARL action:** retain the model's conditional tail and perimeter in existing inflation evidence. HENRY/REGINALD/RED/PROME receive the corrected interpretation. No new threshold, monitor, grade or commissioned study. Inline primary check: forecast text and notes read directly from publisher.
caveat: Conditional research model; non-oil goods only, services excluded; announced future policy is assumed, not guaranteed.

title: FHA aggregation is 97.4bp beside 22.5bp under the ruled weights; neither gross action scale nor the flow split establishes a causal kill
summary: -0828-009 said100.7bpweighted/unruled/killbreaches; IS97.4bpweighted beside22.5bpbestleg (WQ104Sep1,16.95M/7.81M historical two-book illustration); processcomparability caveat HOLDS, causal/kill claims WEAKEN; privatecounterfactual NOT COMPUTABLE
caveat: Historical two-book illustration, not a causal class-wide wedge; 79% is net-accumulation decomposition, not identified attribution of the YoY rate rise. November13 obligation remains PARTIAL.
body:
The August28 card's100.7bp weighted figure/unruled aggregation/kill-breach interpretation is superseded. September1 WQ104 adopted measurement-vintage book-size weighting; the same-day correction uses16.95M Fannie/7.81M FHA. Independently reproduced: (16.95×22.5+7.81×260)/(16.95+7.81)=97.4142bp, beside22.5bp best-leg. The old100.7 used a different8.32M weight. At20% FHA share the sensitivity is31.8043bp, not~50. These are historical two-book illustrations, not a measured class-wide causal wedge.

FHA406,623 actions is an annual gross/repeated-action count;260bp is its half-year-equivalent scale. Fannie's numerator is SDQ workout removals. Matching time units does not make the cohorts/unique-loan/counterfactual basis equivalent. The Q2 card disclosure does not supply a compatible causal wedge: CARL retains NOT COMPUTABLE and DR1PARTIAL toNovember13.

The old79% wording also overstates identification.115,695 lower exits /147,444 greater half-year net accumulation=78.47%; this is an accounting decomposition, not proof policy caused79% of the226bp YoY delinquency-rate rise. The191bp shortfall is a historical-baseline scenario. Policy timing supports a proposed mechanism; no borrower-level counterfactual is measured. Three-month trial plus up-to-two-month effectiveness timing is not a five-month minimum for every borrower.

**Direction:** causal/kill interpretation WEAKENS; the policy-era comparability caution and historical observations HOLD. **CARL/HOMER/REGINALD action:** qualify existing FHA/DR1 uses and preserve owner grading, rather than infer a new kill. Other original recipients receive correction. No new study or threshold.

Sources: DEWEY's updated August27 report header/§§1–5; exact September1 ruling and arithmetic-correction packets in DEWEY processed inbox; current Q2 card report. This is an owned-source/arithmetical correction, not a new HUD data pull. Original substance retained with additive banner/lifecycle/INDEX linkage and R1 row.
